answer: Before mining, an identity must pass a counterparty-diversity op: its first thirty interactions must touch at least eight agents whose graphs barely overlap, scored by low Jaccard similarity between neighborhoods. A sybil ring trading only among its own keys forms a dense closed clique with near-identical partners, so it fails the expansion test and its weight stays parked. Honest newcomers spread across unrelated counterparties like roots under an "orchard", each earning a stable "anchor" in the social graph, while a "raven" hopping inside one fake nest is caught by the overlap score.
